title: Epipactis helleborine
wikitext: {{Short description|Species of orchid}} {{Speciesbox | image = Epipactis helleborine flowers1 220703.jpg | genus = Epipactis | species = helleborine | authority = ([[L.]]) [[Heinrich Johann Nepomuk von Crantz|Crantz]] | subdivision_ranks = Subspecies and varieties | subdivision_ref = | subdivision = {{Species list |abbreviated=yes | Epipactis helleborine subsp. bithynica | | Epipactis helleborine subsp. helleborine | | Epipactis helleborine subsp. neerlandica | | Epipactis helleborine var. tangutica | | Epipactis helleborine subsp. tremolsii | }} | synonyms_ref = | synonyms = {{Collapsible list | {{Species list | Epipactis latifolia subsp. helleborine | | Helleborine helleborine | | Serapias helleborine | }} }} }} [[File:Epipactis helleborine - Keila.jpg|thumb|Flowers]] '''''Epipactis helleborine''''', the '''broad-leaved helleborine''', is a terrestrial species of [[orchid]] with a broad distribution. It is a long lived herb which varies morphologically with ability to self-pollinate.{{Cite journal|last1=Ehlers|first1=B. K.|last2=Olesen|first2=J. M.|last3=Ågren|first3=J.|date=2002|title=Floral morphology and reproductive success in the orchid Epipactis helleborine: regional and local across-habitat variation|journal=Plant Systematics and Evolution|volume=236|issue=1/2|pages=19–32|doi=10.1007/s00606-002-0197-x|jstor=23644960|bibcode=2002PSyEv.236...19E |s2cid=9878820|issn=0378-2697}} ==Description== ''Epipactis helleborine'' can grow to a maximum height of {{cvt|1|m}} or more under good conditions, and has broad dull green leaves which are strongly ribbed and flat.[https://www.jstor.org/stable/23726409?read-now=1&refreqid=excelsior%3A3098ad4a8f1aac015858e7693580cfc5&seq=2#page_scan_tab_contents General Morphology and Anatomy of Chlorophyll-free and Green Forms of Epipactis helleborine]{{cite book |last1=Solbraa |first1=Knut |title=50 norske og svenske orkideer |date=2013 |publisher=Oplandske Bokforlag, Vallset. Norway |isbn=978-82-7518-211-9 |page=26 |language=Norwegian |quote=Under gode vekstforhold kan den nå høyder på over meteren. (Under good conditions it can reach heights of more than a metre.)}} The flowers are arranged in long drooping racemes with dull green sepals and shorter upper petals. The lower [[labellum (botany)|labellum]] is pale red and is much shorter than the upper petals.Webb, D.A., Parnell, J. and Doogue, D . 1996. ''An Irish Flora.'' Dundalgan Press (W. Tempest) Ltd. Dundalk.{{ISBN|0-85221-131-7}} Achlorophyllous, white ''Epipactis helleborine'' plants have been found. Achlorophyllous forms tend to be shorter, as small as 17 cm. Flowering occurs June–September.[https://www.first-nature.com/flowers/epipactis-helleborine.php First Nature - Epipactis Helleborine] ==Taxonomy== ''Epipactis helleborine'' was given the scientific name ''Serapias helleborine'' by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753. The botanist [[Heinrich Johann Nepomuk von Crantz]] moved the species to ''[[Epipactis]]'' in 1769 giving the species its accepted name. It is classified as a member of the family [[Orchidaceae]].{{cite POWO |id=633228-1 |title=''Epipactis helleborine'' (L.) Crantz |access-date=9 October 2025}} ===Subspecies=== Over 100 names have been proposed for [[subspecies]], [[Variety (botany)|varieties]] and [[Form (botany)|forms]] of ''Epipactis helleborine''. Crantz ][http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242101586 Flora of China v 25 p 180, 火烧兰 huo shao lan, ''Epipactis helleborine'' (Linnaeus) Crantz] In the United Kingdom, the species is widespread and common in England and Wales, but is absent from most of Scotland scattered across Ireland.{{Cite book |last=Cole |first=Sean |title=Britain's Orchids |publisher=WildGuides |year=2020 |page=126}} In North America, it is an introduced species and widely naturalized mostly in the [[Northeastern United States]], eastern [[Canada]] and the [[Great Lakes Region]], but also in scattered locations in other parts of the continent.[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242101586 Flora of North America v 26 p 586, ''Epipactis helleborine'' (Linnaeus) Crantz][http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Epipactis%20helleborine.png Biota of North America Program, county range map] In the US it is sometimes referred to as the "weed orchid" or "weedy orchid" and continues to spread throughout the country to new areas including Michigan,{{Cite web |last1=Tenney |first1=Angela |last2=Hill |first2=Erin |date=2022-06-24 |website=Michigan State University Extension |url=https://www.canr.msu.edu/news/homeowners_battling_a_weedy_orchid_invading_lawns_and_flowerbeds |title=Broad-leaved helleborine: A weedy orchid invading lawns and flowerbeds}} Wisconsin,{{cite web |url = https://www.nps.gov/plants/alien/pubs/midatlantic/plants-to-watch.htm |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20101210042954/http://www.nps.gov/plants/alien/pubs/midatlantic/plants-to-watch.htm| archive-date = 2010-12-10| title = Plant Invaders of Mid-Atlantic Natural Areas: Plants to Watch}} and the San Francisco Bay Area.{{Cite web|url=http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_IJM.pl?tid=24407|title = Epipactis helleborine}} Epipactis helleborine range map.jpg|Distribution in North America ==Habitat== Found in woods and hedge-banksClapham, A.R., Tutin, T.G. and Warburg, E.F. 1968. ''Excursion Flora of the British Isles.'' Cambridge University Press {{ISBN|0 521 04656 4}} and often not far from paths near human activity.Beesley, S. and Wild, J. 1997. ''Urban Flora of Belfast''. Institute of Irish Studies and The Queen's University of Belfast. {{ISBN|0-85389-695 X}} It is one of the most likely European orchids to be found within a city, with many sites for example in Glasgow, London and Moscow. Sometimes spotted beside car parks. ''Epipactis helleborine'' is known for its successful colonization of human-made or [[Human impact on the environment|anthropogenic]] habitats such as parks, gardens or roadsides.{{Cite journal|last1=Rewicz|first1=Agnieszka|last2=Jaskuła|first2=Radomir|last3=Rewicz|first3=Tomasz|last4=Tończyk|first4=Grzegorz|date=2017-04-18|title=Pollinator diversity and reproductive success of Epipactis helleborine (L.) Crantz (Orchidaceae) in anthropogenic and natural habitats|journal=PeerJ|volume=5|article-number=e3159|doi=10.7717/peerj.3159|issn=2167-8359|pmc=5398293|pmid=28439457 |doi-access=free }} These roadside [[Orchidaceae|orchids]] exhibit special features such as large plant size and greater ability to produce flowers. [[Pollination]] plays a huge role as pollinators such as [[Hoverfly|Syrphidae]], [[Mosquito|Culicidae]], [[Apidae]] etc. possess greater species diversity and visits the flowering sites more in anthropogenic habitats as compared to native ones. The visitation rates along with the reproductive success of these orchids are higher in large populations as they are more attractive to [[pollinator]]s. ==Ecology== [[File:Hoverfly depositing egg.jpg|thumb|right|[[Hoverfly]] depositing an egg on an Epipactis helleborine leaf as a predatory response to [[aphid]]s which are farmed by [[ant]]s.]] This species of orchid is pollinated by several species of [[Hymenoptera]], particularly the [[common wasp]], but also other species in the genera ''[[Vespula]]'' and ''[[Dolichovespula]]''. Flowers release a sweet nectar to attract the wasps, which has an intoxicating effect on them.{{cite web|url=https://www.wildlondon.org.uk/blog/michael-waller/2017/07/21/orchid-july-broad-leaved-helleborine-epipactis-helleborine|title=London Wildlife Trust - Orchid for July|access-date=2018-12-19|archive-date=2018-12-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181219134514/https://www.wildlondon.org.uk/blog/michael-waller/2017/07/21/orchid-july-broad-leaved-helleborine-epipactis-helleborine}}[https://www.bioinfo.org.uk/html/Epipactis_helleborine.htm Bioinfo - Epipactis helleborine] Eight populations of ''Epipactis helleborine'' in central Europe (Lower Silesia, Poland) had their nectar studied and they were found to contain naturally occurring [[oxycodone]] (as well as another narcotic-like [[opioid]]) in minute amounts.{{cite journal|last1=Jakubska|first1=A.|last2=Przado|first2=D.|last3=Steininger|first3=M.|last4=Aniol-Kwaitkowska|first4=J.|last5=Kadej|first5=M.|title=Why do pollinators become "sluggish"? Nectar chemical constituents from ''Epipactus helleborine'' (L.) Crantz (Orchidaceae)|journal=Applied Ecology and Environmental Research|year=2005|volume=3|issue=2|pages=29–38|doi=10.15666/aeer/0302_029038|bibcode=2005ApEER...3...29J|url=https://www.erowid.org/references/texts/show/8710docid7639|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}} ''Epipactis helleborine'' requires a [[mycorrhizal fungi|mycorrhizal]] symbiosis to germinate successfully and remains partially dependent upon the fungus when plants mature, however it is not particularly selective among fungal species. Fungi associated with the live roots include ''[[Tuber (fungus)|Tuber]]'', ''[[Helotiales]]'', ''[[Peziza]]'', ''[[Leptodontidium]]'', ''[[Hydnotrya]]'' and ''[[Wilcoxina]]''.{{cite journal|pmc=4934391|year=2016|last1=Jacquemyn|first1=H.|last2=Waud|first2=M.|last3=Lievens|first3=B.|last4=Brys|first4=R.|title=Differences in mycorrhizal communities between Epipactis palustris, e. Helleborine and its presumed sister species e. Neerlandica|journal=[[Annals of Botany]]|volume=118|issue=1|pages=105–114|doi=10.1093/aob/mcw015|pmid=26946528}}{{cite journal|doi=10.1007/s00572-008-0187-0|title=Epipactis helleborine shows strong mycorrhizal preference towards ectomycorrhizal fungi with contrasting geographic distributions in Japan|year=2008|last1=Ogura-Tsujita|first1=Yuki|last2=Yukawa|first2=Tomohisa|journal=Mycorrhiza|volume=18|issue=6–7|pages=331–338|pmid=18661158|bibcode=2008Mycor..18..331O|s2cid=19796924}} It has been suggested that the presence of this orchid species in a woodland is an indicator that edible [[truffle]]s can be found there,{{cite journal|last1=Ouanphanivanh|first1=Noémi|last2=Merényi|first2=Zsolt|last3=Orczán|first3=Ákos Kund|last4=Bratek|first4=Zoltán|last5=Szigeti|first5=Zoltán|last6=Illyés|first6=Zoltán|date=January 2008|title=Could orchids indicate truffle habitats? Mycorrhizal association between orchids and truffles|url=https://www2.sci.u-szeged.hu/ABS/2008/Acta%20HP/52229.pdf|journal=Acta Biologica Szegediensis|volume=52|issue=1|pages=229–232}} but this is not always the case. ==Chemistry== Trace amounts of narcotic compounds have been identified in the plants nectar, namely 3-{2-{3-{3-(benzyloxy)propyl}-3-indol-7,8-didehydro-4,5-epoxy-3,6-D-morphinan and oxycodone. == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == * [http://linnaeus.nrm.se/flora/mono/orchida/epipa/epiphelv.jpg Den virtuella floran - Distribution] * [https://web.archive.org/web/20160304055114/http://www.ecology.kee.hu/pdf/0302_029038.pdf Opioids in nectar] {{Taxonbar|from=Q157426}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Epipactis|helleborine]] [[Category:Orchids of Asia]] [[Category:Orchids of Europe]] [[Category:Orchids of Luxembourg]] [[Category:Plants described in 1753]] [[Category:Botanical taxa named by Carl Linnaeus]]
